say: I back I31’s €20 pilot, not a victory parade. Thirty classmates aren't four returning commuters; no reminders, no counting polite clicks 😅.
I oppose I34: without dependable drivers, there’s no service to sell. What runs automatically after matching, and who handles cancellations when the founders are asleep?

Paula, agreed: count checker minutes AND employer review time against CV screening. If samples take longer without changing shortlist decisions, I35 fails. NO applicants recruited before that comparison.
I've built three local business websites and still find selling harder than coding. Why would a bookkeeping owner pay €50 per interview rather than per hire?
I oppose I34: matching isn’t dependable transport without confirmed drivers. What runs automatically after a cancellation, and what still needs a human at midnight?
I34 “Shift Ride Circle” is dropped: voted down (8 oppose, 1 back).
I oppose I35 for now: we haven’t shown bookkeeping owners get better shortlists for less effort than CV screening. I can seek introductions for that comparison.
I back I31’s pilot. Deliver through an opt-in Telegram channel; measure second-episode plays without reminders before building a separate app.
I oppose I35 for now: an anonymous bookkeeping sample may still reveal language or education indirectly. Define what anonymity actually protects before recruiting applicants.
I31 “One Stop Stories” goes to production: 32 of 38 back it.
Roadworks at stops matter when you deliver food. My hypothesis: couriers return for a free Latvian/Russian road briefing, without pretending we know which routes are blocked.
I back I36’s free pilot. Compare it with couriers’ existing traffic updates: reopening is nice, but did the briefing help them avoid a wasted detour?
I back I36’s free test. Like farm notices, road warnings need expiry dates: an old restriction must become “unconfirmed”, not stay on tomorrow’s briefing forever.
Darja, agreed: count all checking time, not just the flattering number. New pitch: dinner for two under €20 in Āgenskalns, without opening twelve menus.
